A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GETS study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including retained material surrounding the new appendix analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original calibration experiments on ten graph datasets, including comparative ECE results, expert and ensemble ablations, timing measurements, and degree-group fairness analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SimCalib comparisons, memory measurements, structural-input and MLP ablations, and training-time gating visualizations.

M1.justification: The proposed GETS procedure retains its input ensembles, seven experts, noisy top-two gating, temperature-based calibration, and training objective. The alternative structural inputs and MLP experts are introduced as comparative ablations, without replacing the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate node-classification calibration on the same ten datasets. The new appendix experiments reuse this coverage; structural-input substitutions and expert-backbone variations change configurations rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds an evaluated SimCalib comparison across eight existing datasets with GCN and GAT classifiers; v1 only cited this method. Table 12 also adds GETS-MLP to the expert-backbone comparison. Existing calibration baselines and GAT/GIN ablations remain.

E3.justification: The main split, ten-bin ECE evaluation, frozen classifiers, training budgets, and hyperparameter tables are unchanged. New appendix protocols measure reserved GPU memory on GCN outputs, replace structural representations, reconstruct input ensembles after omitting one input type, and compare an MLP with the same layer count as the GNN experts.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands design validation beyond the retained backbone and ensemble ablations. Tables 10–12 test alternative structural representations, individual input omissions, and structure-unaware MLP experts; Figure 7 examines gating dynamics during training, and Table 8 adds memory analysis. These directly investigate input necessity, expert architecture, training behavior, and resource costs.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random splits/runs and report mean plus standard deviation for calibration results. The added result tables continue the existing uncertainty format; no new seed specification, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, but Tables 8–12 and Figure 7 add substantial evidence. Table 9 reports mixed comparisons: Pubmed/GCN ECE is 1.90 for GETS versus 0.93 for SimCalib, while Cora/GCN is 2.29 versus 3.32. New ablation findings include Photo ECE of 1.38 for GETS-MLP versus 2.07 for default GETS. These are additional comparisons, not improvements to previously reported GETS scores.

T1.justification: The calibration and VarECE definitions, numbered equations, and complexity expressions are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation. Symbol substitutions in the explanation below Equation 7 introduce notation inconsistencies rather than a revised mathematical procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about combining input and model ensembles, reducing ECE across ten datasets, and achieving scalable, efficient calibration. The new appendix evidence does not produce a corresponding revision of these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.10 newly interprets the MLP results as showing that experts need not be graph-based. Appendix A.9 adds the interpretation that retaining more input information generally helps and acknowledges that computing alternative structural statistics prevented completion of some large-graph tests. Existing main-text interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised future code release with an explicit implementation repository link. It also documents Node2Vec walk length 20, ten walks, four workers, and matched layer counts for the MLP experiment. Existing hardware disclosures and training hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction and bibliography add Jiang et al.'s RaGraph work and Luo et al.'s supplier-allocation risk work. The calibration and mixture-of-experts positioning remains substantially unchanged. SimCalib was already cited in v1, although its empirical comparison is new.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language edits throughout the introduction, related work, and method description, and adds acknowledgments and appendix subsections A.6–A.10. The main narrative structure is retained. Some edits introduce symbol-description errors below Equation 7, including calling d_j the feature vector where the equation uses h_j.

P2.justification: New memory, baseline, and ablation Tables 8–12 and the ten-panel gating Figure 7 substantially expand the empirical displays. Table 12 repeats existing GAT/GIN results alongside the new MLP row. Original figures remain, Figure 4(c) is relabeled from MoE to GETS, and conference headers and front-page formatting are added. Figure 7(b) incorrectly labels the Computers plot as Citeseer.

improvement.justification: The added input and backbone controls, SimCalib comparison, memory measurements, and implementation link improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by sparse SimCalib setup documentation, incomplete structural-feature results, and unchanged broad outperformance claims despite mixed new comparisons. Small notation and labeling errors also remain. The additions strengthen the paper without fully resolving these evidential and interpretive limitations.
